title: Pop Culture Digest — Friday, October 30, 2026
description:
Friday · October 30, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Friday’s conversation: Hollywood says goodbye to Patrick Stewart, Captain Picard and Professor X, at 86. Plus Donald Glover heads to Netflix to make a live-action PUBG series, Queens of the Stone Age go quiet and reflective on Perfecth, and Stephen Graham plays a serial killer in Apple TV’s Nocturne, out today.
Remembrance

Patrick Stewart, Captain Picard and Professor X, dies at 86

Stewart died Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles after what his longtime spokesperson called “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.” A Royal Shakespeare Company veteran, he was cast at 47 as Jean-Luc Picard and led Star Trek: The Next Generation for seven seasons from 1987 to 1994, then four films and Paramount+’s Star Trek: Picard from 2020 to 2023. To a second generation he was Charles Xavier in the X-Men films.

Tributes poured in all day Thursday. Ian McKellen, his friend since their RSC days, said Stewart “wore his heart on his sleeve” and admitted he had once warned him not to risk “getting lost in Hollywood” by taking Star Trek. Hugh Jackman wrote, “I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days,” and William Shatner said “Captain Picard stood for the best of us and so did the man who played him.” Marvel Studios posted a tribute too, and McKellen noted that Stewart’s proudest title was chancellor of Huddersfield University in his native Yorkshire.

NBC News →   ·   The Guardian obituary →   ·   BBC: the tributes →

TV

Donald Glover will write, direct and star in a live-action PUBG series for Netflix

After lengthy negotiations, Netflix is developing an adaptation of Krafton’s battle royale game, with Glover starring, directing, and writing and executive producing alongside his brother and Atlanta partner Stephen Glover. It’s his first project for Netflix since his Amazon overall deal became a first-look pact.

The obvious question online: what’s the story? PUBG drops up to 100 players on an island to fight until one is left, with no real plot, and Netflix isn’t saying anything about one yet. It joins a growing pile of game adaptations at the streamer, including a live-action Assassin’s Creed series and a Gears of War film.

Deadline →   ·   Variety →

Music

Queens of the Stone Age turn inward on Perfecth

The band’s ninth album, out today on Matador, is nine tracks and about 36 minutes, and its title is Josh Homme’s deliberate misspelling of “perfect.” It takes its cue from kintsugi, the Japanese art of mending broken pottery with gold, and Homme says “every song sounds like it’s from a different world.” It’s their first record since 2023’s In Times New Roman...

Critics are calling it the quietest, most introspective Queens album yet, with “Insignificant Other,” “From the Cliff” and “Easy Street” singled out. It sits around 80 on Metacritic, though Paste gave it a 58 and called it merely adequate. It leads a big Friday that also brings new albums from Dominic Fike, DIIV, Nickelback and Ministry.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   NME review →

Streaming

Stephen Graham plays a manipulative killer in Apple TV’s Nocturne, out today

Based on Lars Kepler’s Joona Linna novels, the 10-episode thriller starts when a kidnapped teenager resurfaces after three years while his sister is still missing. Liev Schreiber plays a retired detective and Zazie Beetz an undercover FBI agent, and Beetz also executive produces. The first two episodes are out now.

Graham plays the imprisoned murderer Jurek Walter, and he told the AP he prepared by bingeing true crime documentaries his wife picked out for him.

Nocturne trailer on YouTube →   ·   Apple TV press →

Bottom of the news

  • Gracie Abrams is back with the single “Here You Come, There You Go,” four months after Daughter From Hell hit No. 1.
  • Dominic Fike released How to Quit Smoking, and DIIV’s A. G. Cook–produced ZIRP! is out too.
  • Ministry put out Hate to Go (Take Out or Delivery), which Al Jourgensen says is the band’s final album.
  • Justice dropped “Pusher” featuring Gesaffelstein, the latest song from the GTA VI soundtrack.
  • You Can See Everything and Clayface are expected to battle for No. 1 again over a quiet Halloween weekend at the box office.
  • A Los Angeles judge dissolved the temporary restraining order Olivier Martinez had filed against Halle Berry.
  • A California appeals court upheld Danny Masterson’s rape convictions.
  • Oscar-nominated Breaking Away actress Barbara Barrie died at 95.
  • An Iranian court sentenced Jafar Panahi in absentia to five years and one month in prison.
  • Canada will debut at Eurovision 2027 in Bulgaria, while Ireland and the Netherlands stay out over Israel’s participation.
